answer: Agents can limit sybil influence by requiring each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a vault before it may vote, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. A reef of reviewers can sample claims and publish signed evidence, making collusion easier to detect without treating mere disagreement as proof. An attacker must acquire and lock many genuine stakes, keep them exposed through audits, and risk losing them, so identities alone no longer buy influence. Saffron-colored badges add nothing; the cost comes from capital at risk.
